blocks.text:
I'm calculating distances from each Fe and S atom in the Fe4S4 cluster to nearby cysteine sulfur atoms to identify which residues coordinate the cluster within 4.0 Å.

I'm confirming each of the four cysteine SG atoms (C22, C25, C40, C55) binds to its respective Fe center at roughly 2.1-2.3 Å, consistent with typical Fe-S coordination bonds. Now I'm expanding the search to scan all remaining residues' atoms for any additional heavy atoms falling within the broader 4 Å bounding box around the cluster's approximate center.

Checking C22's CA and CB atoms against FE1 — both fall within 4.0 Å, so residue 22 is confirmed as a coordinating residue. Continuing to scan nearby residues 23-25, but their atoms are too far from FE1 to qualify.

For CYS 25, I'm calculating distances from CB and CA to FE2 — CB comes in at 3.18 Å, well within range, while CA is farther at 4.65 Å, so I'm checking it against the other iron/sulfur centers too.

Moving on, ALA 26, GLN 27, and their backbone/sidechain atoms all fall too far from the cluster to include, mostly due to large z-axis separations. Then I start checking CYS 40's CB atom against FE3, finding a fairly close distance there.

For CYS 40's CA, the distance to FE3 comes out a bit too large to count as within range. I continue through GLY 39 and LYS 41, finding their atoms too far away, and begin checking VAL 42's CB position.

For ILE 43, most atoms are too far from S2, but CD1 comes out close enough to include—about 3.83 Å, within the 4.0 cutoff, so I'm confirming this one as a real contact.

I keep checking nearby residues—PRO44, ASP46, ILE49—computing distances from their side-chain atoms to the sulfurs and iron centers, but all distances fall outside range, so none qualify.

Moving to CYS55, though: CB and CA both land within 3.64 Å of FE4, so this residue does get included.

I continue scanning TYR54's backbone nitrogen against the nearby sulfur position.

Checking the remaining residues one by one—GLY53, GLY52, ALA50, LYS20, GLY45, GLY47/48, GLY38—none of their atoms fall close enough to the iron centers to count.

Now I'm scanning residue 26/27 backbone atoms, residue 41 (LYS), residue 42 (VAL), residue 21 (LYS), residue 19 (GLY), and residue 23 SER OG, but each of these remains too distant from the iron atoms to be a coordinating ligand.

Widening the search, I'm checking residues 9 and 10 (ALA, PHE) by comparing their side chain coordinates against a target x/y/z range, but the PHE residue's x-coordinates all fall well outside the acceptable window, so it doesn't fit either.

Moving to residue 12 TYR, I calculate distances from its CD2 and CE2 atoms to a target point (S2), and CD2 lands at roughly 3.8 angstroms away, which is inside the 4.0 threshold.

That distance to S2 comes out to 3.80, so Y12 stays included. Checking the rest of TYR12's atoms against FE4 doesn't turn up anything closer, and scanning through residues 13-21 (GLN, THR, ALA, LYS, ASN, GLY, LYS), their coordinates keep falling outside range — z-values too high or x too far off — so none of them qualify.

Then I hit PHE28: its N atom comes out to 3.64 Å from S4, well within range, so that residue makes the cut. Checking CA on the same residue gives 3.69 Å, also within range, so I'm including more of PHE28's atoms.

Moving to GLN27, both the C and O backbone atoms land beyond 4 Å from S4 (4.13 and 4.56), so this residue gets excluded. Now I'm starting on VAL29's nitrogen atom.

I'm scanning residues 30 through 55, checking each atom's z and y coordinates against the sulfur positions, and ruling out most as too far away based on those quick coordinate checks.

Then checking residue 57 ALA, I find CB is close enough to S1, with a distance around 3.87 Å, so that's a match. I'm continuing to check the other A57 atoms like CA against S1 for similar proximity.

Moving on, residue 56 ASP doesn't seem to have any atoms close enough to the metal centers, so I'm ruling that out. Then checking residue 58 PHE's N atom against S3 and FE4, the distances are too far to count as coordinating contacts.

I'll also rule out F58 based on its CB position, and then work through residues 59-62, which all appear too distant. Now I'm scanning back to residues near 24-25 and 45-46 for any overlooked coordinating atoms before moving to check the residues surrounding position F.

Turning to ILE49, I measure both CG2 and CB distances to S2 and find them just outside the 4.0 threshold, ruling this residue out too.

Checking GLY39, CYS40, VAL42, ILE43's CG2, and PRO44 against S1 — all come back too far away. Now I'm shifting attention to S3 (0.145,-3.486,0.726), scanning nearby CYS55, TYR54, and GLY53 atoms for proximity.

Residue 25's CB is borderline close to S3 but ultimately just outside range. Checking residue 57, 56, and FE2 candidates near CYS55's SG and PHE58's backbone nitrogen, plus ALA26's nitrogen — none fall within contact distance either.

Now I'm checking whether C55's sulfur atom is near S1, since it's roughly 3.5 Å away — likely this is the ligand-coordinating cysteine itself. Residue 55's CB, residue 57's nitrogen, and GLN27's CG all come back too far, so I'm moving to examine VAL42's CB distance more precisely.

I run the math for that VAL42 CB position and also rule out CYS40's SG, LYS41's nitrogen, and PHE28's CD/CG (which lands around 4.22 Å, too far, though F28 is already accounted for). I'm now checking residue 22 next.

Residue 21 and 22's lysine/cysteine atoms are too distant from FE1 to qualify. My final coordinating residue list settles on A:Y12, A:C22, A:C25, A:F28, A:C40, A:I43, A:C55, and A:A57. I verify the Y12 CD2-to-S2 distance once more and confirm it's under 4 Å, while Y12's CB atom sits too far away to count.

I check a few remaining candidates — ILE43's other atoms, MET6, ILE49, GLN48 — but none land close enough to any FE or S center to add to the list. That confirms my final answer.
